Dihydromyricetin (DHM) is a plant flavonoid—most commonly derived from *Hovenia dulcis* (Japanese raisin tree) or *Ampelopsis grossedentata* —marketed in hangover remedies and liver-support supplements.  [Highlight start] Preclinical studies suggest it interacts with brain receptors and liver enzymes tied to alcohol, though **strong human clinical evidence is still limited** [Highlight end].[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbgHEIkXXsfZE5JsK5aMyYVeOflB3Z-YoxkII4AGqq1oIzxyVJCEa5IHV6QieDyqJdZCv5GCNHGhD8EsOOC4WG8SRQAM26KNzHjpiC6yHaS_yfv-dqceyYDa0A32NQUgV5nH7jdZCR9BJ2Ojlfp9C)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESggEBxCJF13LeZvSloBqe5WAnn1mZdRcvqHA8I7oVLnhxNAxWfmkqTfW0L8BlSnfq_njqpgVseeXtBHZjzcGB0MW_TQ-EpysADm5nu-gdOFtFpqAbDHRJ06ksW9mhuUNwCbR2E6E77tvzG1LKalFqvYvwlRpvlf-yAFh1fQRwRdrbaUfX)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESaQHEIkXXT0ngJFZEdi-vZ4lBNZNNdlur9hTA9NOCjuxpBdCtueruAGjyNV2ptXwqf4d1ueAuxk7efr559mnTnfdxPqgwxWjbzXunNuAeEgVMGWLnBEtXf7VZgVaXE1spOHsL0NH_vJH_Og)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkwEBxCJF1-BoqMRE1KiU80LlOZST_0_baF0ev_30F_odCAOls1xSHJ820ufBUjX1XZj6-lQILvsDr1rUJQUNeDcd-eJpOcheTlmlv_geIWF64T_ir0PCc2NMPZDy0u_HDxb5ypbymusvUdU7S4_T3VHwhRy54Frnx5Kok8yOnZXWOdJ9r-N_emEjieeDepOmUSggjRk)[[5]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESggEBxCJF12hNTtIvttzUiTT9nT_xLlM5CThxtW1pR18ALr_BG-I9miI1FNpMMKL74JwUoRGVMgH9dLW6QzLeu2hBy3xr6PAlTIbRSGs7KvOWr9Um2V4xGrTVtYuVKm3ya3C3expOtCP8DL9XxGZ0TlFY5d578OUs_feKB4UKCBeiFI4v)

### How It Is Studied With Alcohol

- **Brain receptors (GABA-A):** Animal and cell studies suggest DHM can counteract some effects of alcohol on GABA-A receptors, which are involved in intoxication, tolerance, and withdrawal symptoms.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbgHEIkXXsfZE5JsK5aMyYVeOflB3Z-YoxkII4AGqq1oIzxyVJCEa5IHV6QieDyqJdZCv5GCNHGhD8EsOOC4WG8SRQAM26KNzHjpiC6yHaS_yfv-dqceyYDa0A32NQUgV5nH7jdZCR9BJ2Ojlfp9C)
- **Alcohol breakdown & liver protection:** Preclinical research indicates DHM may reduce oxidative stress and inflammation in liver cells and influence alcohol-metabolizing enzymes (such as ADH, ALDH, and CYP2E1), though findings on actual alcohol metabolism rates vary across animal models.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbgHEIkXXY2jMZiwOOWz6IYE2Sa7V5UKVLHh__DSKDNISVvFkHMm75WW_qFqyAaY1yN4v7USZSwaogs_O2NBUHzXsGXgJoLAtsFD2SCRgikCZ8dWSeF0FRRYnZps0fmtTozbRGm8hSSkz9VfgWJsn)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESggEBxCJF13LeZvSloBqe5WAnn1mZdRcvqHA8I7oVLnhxNAxWfmkqTfW0L8BlSnfq_njqpgVseeXtBHZjzcGB0MW_TQ-EpysADm5nu-gdOFtFpqAbDHRJ06ksW9mhuUNwCbR2E6E77tvzG1LKalFqvYvwlRpvlf-yAFh1fQRwRdrbaUfX)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkwEBxCJF1-BoqMRE1KiU80LlOZST_0_baF0ev_30F_odCAOls1xSHJ820ufBUjX1XZj6-lQILvsDr1rUJQUNeDcd-eJpOcheTlmlv_geIWF64T_ir0PCc2NMPZDy0u_HDxb5ypbymusvUdU7S4_T3VHwhRy54Frnx5Kok8yOnZXWOdJ9r-N_emEjieeDepOmUSggjRk)
- **Human research:** While DHM has a long history in traditional Asian herbal teas, controlled human trials on safety, dosing, and effectiveness for hangovers or alcohol-related liver conditions remain early-stage.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESaQHEIkXXT0ngJFZEdi-vZ4lBNZNNdlur9hTA9NOCjuxpBdCtueruAGjyNV2ptXwqf4d1ueAuxk7efr559mnTnfdxPqgwxWjbzXunNuAeEgVMGWLnBEtXf7VZgVaXE1spOHsL0NH_vJH_Og)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESjwEBxCJF1-QK_AaCn0vc8HU1_po9ci4pRZSidxrU0tCVpYC7V4CtYsLBq8VJT6V_ZL9jTzVNI0G1kCNWqYz2A7NhOF_7AK_5_Tzawvvv1400X7L8QYQtCoXvv1v8sqIUvI-3gx_Sw3NGngo1ax6rqF8Bj6pfUORgy9Bdf4PVQeD5DWFbJ-Yt5g3S55OlYs6mww)

### Practical Limitations & Safety

- **Not a safety net:** DHM does not reliably prevent intoxication, sober you up safely, or eliminate the health risks of alcohol.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESggEBxCJF12hNTtIvttzUiTT9nT_xLlM5CThxtW1pR18ALr_BG-I9miI1FNpMMKL74JwUoRGVMgH9dLW6QzLeu2hBy3xr6PAlTIbRSGs7KvOWr9Um2V4xGrTVtYuVKm3ya3C3expOtCP8DL9XxGZ0TlFY5d578OUs_feKB4UKCBeiFI4v)
- **Supplement regulation:** In the U.S., DHM is sold as a dietary supplement rather than an FDA-approved drug for alcohol use or hangovers, meaning ingredient amounts and purity can vary across products.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgAEBxCJF18r1CFBCt5omBPB_xYNTcnbyjCRdgO-GSfGh_uXqglT2Z30xiIlPe12OchL6xNylBAAJkzTYgVGJXFa9BkrEIIh7hYEZs0Gh6HVgzdsHdRobOpqVQzZlSenIP3CRn0TvB8Q6gPsGeXkn7_pZq2xIRiZe8cadYaTLvmhk8Q)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESggEBxCJF12hNTtIvttzUiTT9nT_xLlM5CThxtW1pR18ALr_BG-I9miI1FNpMMKL74JwUoRGVMgH9dLW6QzLeu2hBy3xr6PAlTIbRSGs7KvOWr9Um2V4xGrTVtYuVKm3ya3C3expOtCP8DL9XxGZ0TlFY5d578OUs_feKB4UKCBeiFI4v)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESaQHEIkXXT0ngJFZEdi-vZ4lBNZNNdlur9hTA9NOCjuxpBdCtueruAGjyNV2ptXwqf4d1ueAuxk7efr559mnTnfdxPqgwxWjbzXunNuAeEgVMGWLnBEtXf7VZgVaXE1spOHsL0NH_vJH_Og)
- **Anecdotal reports:** Opinions on [Reddit](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEShQEBxCJF18A_HLVTgwhZjfXvu9mupz15P67IDM-hz3Vl6WyHzkpfxEKFdSN_6luOrUJOAL7_y6PquduucK_8HKM_6Jdc003TnbNf0VODHFCKNvDJ91Ik4Tx5l-E0_BFvwlQl6C4Mh3Iwp4dAsEnpX1hlGJMunV89lzbLo-Ji5OZbyAAbHdS-) are mixed—some users report feeling little to no buzz or reduced intoxication after taking DHM before drinking, while others notice a milder or capped buzz, and some point out the risk of drinking more if intoxication feels blunted.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEShQEBxCJF18A_HLVTgwhZjfXvu9mupz15P67IDM-hz3Vl6WyHzkpfxEKFdSN_6luOrUJOAL7_y6PquduucK_8HKM_6Jdc003TnbNf0VODHFCKNvDJ91Ik4Tx5l-E0_BFvwlQl6C4Mh3Iwp4dAsEnpX1hlGJMunV89lzbLo-Ji5OZbyAAbHdS-)
